newsitem.title: SPAIN: Employers' jobs stance unacceptable - Spain union.
newsitem.headline: Employers' jobs stance unacceptable - Spain union.

text.p: A top Spanish union official said on Tuesday that employers' position in labour reform negotiations remained unacceptable to the unions.

Employers want unfair dismissal costs reduced to 25 days for each year worked with a maximum outlay of 12 months salary. Companies must currently pay 45 days for each year worked. They also want more flexibility in dismissal grounds.

"It is perfectly understandable why unions reject this," UGT Secretary for Union Action Toni Ferrer told Spanish national radio. "Because it would be tantamount to destroying employment and the possibilites for stable employment in our country."
Employers will shortly make public their final offer and will present it to unions at final talks at midday.
The conservative Popular Party government has said it will step in if the two sides fail to reach agreement on reform.
